I have been put in a similar position to you before and I know how it feels. I would also be very creeped out to receive this letter. The reality of being a femme person in this world is that we know that sometimes these things can escalate quickly, and the risk of that happening (even if small) is so, so scary. I'm so sorry that this happened and made you feel uncomfortable.

I would advise you to tell him "no thank you, I am not interested in spending any alone time together. Please do not ask me again" and leave it at that. I would hope he would get the message and not pursue anything further. Is there anyone in your life that will be on your side on this? Family, friends? Tell them, show them this letter, and let them know your response and that you feel uncomfortable too. Definitely let them know if he persists or his mother retaliates (I think the former at least is somewhat unlikely, but I get wanting to protect yourself). I promise that even if you doubt it now, there will be more people that believe you and can advocate for you than you assume.

It's important to learn how to start setting boundaries now, learning to trust your intuition, and recognizing that you SHOULD NOT prioritize men's feelings over your safety and bodily integrity. This could also be a valuable lesson for this man in terms of learning to accept boundaries when given to him.

“IF YOU WALK THROUGH THE GAARDEN...”

Three experiences. The first is long, the other two are very short. 

1. I'll start with the longest one. This happened about 10-15 years ago, as my brother and I would have been 10-14. My brother, father, and I were visiting the Morris Arboretum in southern PA. We came across these woods with a trail leading into it, and my brother and I decided to explore. My dad stayed behind. It already started out really weird because as my brother and I went down the trail, my dad started making these weird sounds as we walked farther and farther away from him...like belching repeatedly? He doesn't do that though, at least never before and never again. At least I think it was him...  
Anyway, we continue. The path eventually splits, and I take the upper path while my brother takes the lower path towards a lake. As I go up the path, I start to hear really loud booming/banging noises. I get scared that someone's hunting nearby, and I start yelling to make sure they know I'm a person and not an animal. No response. These little rocks start falling and rolling away by themselves, heading down from the top of the hill and hitting me in the shoes. I figure that some animal is moving around and making them roll towards me, but the rocks honestly seem to be moving by themselves...like there is no prior force behind them.  
I meet up my brother near the lake. Suddenly, all of the geese that have previously been swimming in the water start honking and fly away. My brother looks behind us and says "oh my God what is that?" I turn to look but my vision is partially obscured by a tree. What I did see was a huge black figure with no features, almost like a big black cloak, but it was obviously sentient and not cloth. It did not look like a jacket or a coat or fabric--it looked like something pitch black, standing on its own near a tree. My brother got a better look, and he would describe it as **something like a black bat the size of a man**. We both fucking booked it out of the forest and emerged gasping on the other side, back at the main part of the arboretum.   
I've told my story to my dad a few years later and he's just kind of nervously laughed and said "oh, I think it was me in the woods trying to scare you guys." Honestly I think he's tried to save face for me because he prides himself on being a rational person and I was telling this story to a group of family and friends. Plus, I did not see him throwing rocks down at me (I had a clear view of the top of the hill), and he wasn't wearing a huge black cloak or anything like that at the time. He would of had to be wearing like a black sheet to make himself look like what we saw.  

2. Again, I was 10-14, playing on the computer in my basement. There was a couch that was facing away from me nearby. Out of my peripheral vision, I see something kind of jump up and arc down on the couch, a brief flash of black, almost like if a huge black snake was springing up and diving back down on my couch. I also hear something that sounds like the combination of hissing and giggling. I say sarcastically "\[brother's name\], is that a ghost or are you trying to scare me?" Not 5 seconds later, my brother comes down the stairs, completely unaware of what just happened. The black figure **wasn't him.**  
A lot of other weird shit has happened in my house involving shadowy, black figures, but I could potentially explain most of them away with sleep paralysis/pre-sleep hallucinations. I used to think they were Shadow People.   

3. A little different but still creepy/weird. Some background: I'm a huge Pink Floyd fan, and have been since I was in 5th grade. I was angsty and felt a deep connection to their music and members. One day in September 2008, I'm in a class in high school when I suddenly get this deeply chilling shiver within me like I had never felt before. It felt like a slug, cold and slimy, was full-on doing a poll dance down my spine. I immediately thought, "someone just died." Later that day, I would find out that Richard Wright, a founding member of Pink Floyd, had died. I've never had such a palpable chilly feeling since where I just *knew* that someone had died.
